title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Rebound swell rolls in after last week's AI wipeout
conditions.summary: Futures are bouncing hard, led by the Nasdaq, after the S&P 500 closed Friday in a correction. Volatility is still high, so the water is choppy even as the swell builds.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are up about 2.6% and Dow futures about 1.8% in early trading; quotes are early and moving around between sources.
Nasdaq-100 futures lead with a gain of about 3.5%, and Russell 2000 futures are up about 2.4%.
The bounce follows a brutal week: the S&P 500 closed Friday more than 10% below its October record, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% on Friday alone.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.91%, the dollar index is little changed near 103.9, and the VIX ended Friday near 30.
WTI crude is slightly lower near $83 a barrel despite Gulf shipping attacks; gold is up about 3% near $3,620 and bitcoin is steady near $61,400.
Asia was mixed: Japan was closed for a holiday, South Korea's Kospi fell about 3.3%, Taiwan rose about 2.2%, and Hong Kong and Shanghai were roughly flat.
Europe is higher in early trade, with the FTSE 100, CAC 40 and DAX each up about half a percent.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: Chicago Fed National Activity Index for October.
8:45 AM CT: S&P Global flash PMIs for November; manufacturing forecast near 54.5 and services near 55.6.
Treasury auctions 3- and 6-month bills at 10:30 AM CT and 2-year notes at noon CT.
3:00 PM CT: New York Fed President John Williams speaks; the last Fed meeting of the year is December 8-9.
The main story is whether last week's AI-led selloff was a flush-out or the start of something bigger; this holiday week's data will be the test.

sections.title: Earnings
items: No major reports landed between Friday's close and this morning.
Gap rose more than 11% on Friday after a quarterly profit beat, even though it trimmed its full-year outlook.
After today's close: Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Agilent, Zoom, Trip.com, Symbotic and Jacobs report.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NBIS (Nebius Group): +9.8% — bouncing after a 16% drop on Friday as AI infrastructure names rebound.
APLD (Applied Digital): +8.8% — AI data-center stock recovers part of Friday's nearly 18% slide.
HUT (Hut 8): +8.6% — crypto miner and AI host rebounds with the group after Friday's selloff.
IREN (IREN Ltd): +8.2% — rebounds after an 18% Friday drop.
AAOI (Applied Optoelectronics): +8.3% — optical networking supplier bounces with AI hardware.
CIFR (Cipher Digital): +8.0% — another AI and crypto infrastructure name recovering.
NVDA (Nvidia): higher pre-market — rebounding after a 14% fall on Friday; chip names Micron and SanDisk are also up.
HDB (HDFC Bank): -1.5% — Indian bank slips as India's Sensex falls about 1.7%.

sections.title: Business News
items: Last week the Nasdaq and Dow posted their biggest weekly declines in more than six years as investors pulled back from AI stocks.
Anthropic, which began trading on Thursday, fell 8.5% on Friday as the selloff spread.
Oil is being held up by shipping attacks in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz, and a Houthi claim of an attack on a Saudi refinery.
Global Payments jumped about 10% on Friday on reports that private-equity firm GTCR is exploring a takeover.
University of Michigan consumer sentiment improved sharply in November, slightly better than expected.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 8:30 AM CT open: can the futures bounce hold, or does it fade the way rebounds did last week?
8:45 AM CT flash PMIs: a read on whether the economy is still running hot.
After the close: Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Zoom, a first look at AI server and software demand this week.

sections.title: Earnings This Week
items: Mon: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), after close — AI server orders and margins.
Mon: Zoom (ZM), after close — growth and AI features.
Tue: Analog Devices (ADI), before open — industrial and auto chip demand.
Tue: Medtronic (MDT), before open — medical device growth.
Tue: Best Buy (BBY), before open — holiday sales outlook under its new CEO.
Tue: Dollar Tree (DLTR), before open — low-income shopper and tariff effects.
Tue: Dell Technologies (DELL), after close — AI server revenue; the biggest report of the week.
Tue: Workday (WDAY), after close — software demand amid AI worries.
Tue: Autodesk (ADSK), after close — design software subscriptions.
Tue: HP Inc. (HPQ), after close — PC demand and costs.
Wed: Deere (DE), before open — whether farm equipment has hit bottom.
Wed: Li Auto (LI), before open — China EV demand.

sections.title: Economic Calendar This Week
items: Mon 8:45 AM CT: S&P Global flash PMIs (Nov) — services prior 56.1, manufacturing prior 54.9.
Mon 3:00 PM CT: New York Fed President Williams speaks.
Tue 9:00 AM CT: Conference Board consumer confidence (Nov) — prior 91.7.
Wed 7:30 AM CT: Q3 GDP second estimate — forecasts near 3.4%.
Wed 7:30 AM CT: October personal income, spending and PCE inflation — core PCE prior 3.1% y/y.
Wed 7:30 AM CT: Durable goods orders (Oct) and weekly jobless claims, moved up a day for the holiday.
Wed 9:00 AM CT: New home sales; 1:00 PM CT: Fed Beige Book.
Thu: Markets closed for Thanksgiving.
Fri: Stocks close early at noon CT; Black Friday kicks off the holiday shopping season.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, November twenty third, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Gus the wonder dog is on the deck with me this morning, and he is ready for Thanksgiving week. Give us a holiday howdy, Gus! Alright, let's paddle out. Last week was one gnarly wipeout. The S and P five hundred closed Friday in a correction, more than ten percent below its October record, and the Nasdaq dropped over five percent on Friday alone. But this morning the swell is back. S and P futures are up about two point six percent. Nasdaq futures are up about three and a half percent. Dow futures are up almost two percent, and the Russell two thousand is up about two point four percent. These are early quotes, so expect some chop. The ten year Treasury yield sits near four point nine one percent. The dollar is flat. Crude oil is a touch lower near eighty three dollars, gold is up about three percent, and bitcoin is steady near sixty one thousand. The fear gauge, the VIX, ended Friday near thirty, so the water is still rough. Overseas, Japan was closed, South Korea fell over three percent, and Europe is up about half a percent. On the weather map today, the Chicago Fed activity index lands at seven thirty A M Central, and flash readings on manufacturing and services come out at eight forty five. New York Fed President John Williams speaks at three P M Central. On the tide chart, no big reports came in overnight. After today's close, we hear from Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Zoom, Agilent and Trip dot com. In the lineup, the A I infrastructure crowd that got pounded Friday is bouncing. Nebius is up almost ten percent, Applied Digital is up about nine percent, and Hut eight, Iren and Cipher Digital are each up around eight percent. Nvidia is higher too, after a fourteen percent drop on Friday. Now that is a stock catching a wave. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Just remember, a one day bounce is not a trend, so don't drop in like a kook. In beach talk, oil is getting support from shipping attacks in the Gulf, and Global Payments jumped Friday on takeover reports. Sets to watch today: whether the bounce holds after the eight thirty open, the eight forty five flash readings, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise tonight. Now for the week's swell forecast. It's a short holiday week. Tuesday is the big earnings day. Before the open we get Analog Devices, Medtronic, Best Buy and Dollar Tree. After the close come Dell, Workday, Autodesk and H P. Wednesday morning brings Deere and Li Auto. Wednesday is also the big data day. At seven thirty A M Central we get third quarter G D P, October P C E inflation, durable goods and jobless claims, all at once. New home sales follow at nine, and the Fed's Beige Book lands at one P M Central. Thursday the market is closed for Thanksgiving, and Friday stocks close early at noon Central. The two biggest waves to watch are Dell's A I server numbers on Tuesday and the P C E inflation report on Wednesday. Stay stoked, stay a soul surfer, and keep your board waxed. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
